title: Real geometry engine adapter and model viewport
objective: Integrate the first real geometry engine behind the frozen CAD/BIM adapter boundary (Architecture v1.1, LOCK-003/018). Replace the dummy geometry implementation with a production adapter for the validated FreeCAD/OCCT candidate while preserving engine independence of the renderer, CADDocument, and App API. Support a minimal canonical geometry set — box, cylinder, transform, boolean fuse/cut, selection/query metadata — and deterministic serialization of adapter state sufficient for the existing CADDocument workflow. Connect the Web and Electron workspace surfaces to the real adapter through the same App API; host code remains transport-specific only. Engine processes remain isolated according to the CAD-005 performance findings: bounded workers/timeouts, no engine imports in the renderer, and typed adapter failures. The Construction Graph remains the canonical system of record; CADDocument remains the editor representation (LOCK-019). The dummy adapter remains the permanent test double.
acceptance_criteria: Real geometry adapter satisfies the existing EngineAdapterBundle contract without changing its public semantic meaning (app/src/contracts/adapter.ts byte-unchanged: adapterMark 'offisos:adapter-boundary:1', async prepareGeometry/extractSemantics/read/write).

Renderer/App API has zero direct FreeCAD/OCCT imports: the forbidden-import static check (LOCK-018) stays green and the real engine code lives only under the concrete adapter/worker layer (app/src/adapters/occt/).
Dummy adapter remains fully functional and testable: the existing 50-test suite stays green, byte-identical.
Web and Electron execute the same representative geometry workflow (geometry.prepare -> applyEdit(addElement) through the shared App API) and yield identical results.
Geometry results are deterministic within declared tolerances: identical geometry recipes produce identical meshTokens and bboxes across processes, runs, and hosts.

Typed failures cover invalid geometry and engine/process failure boundaries: engine_timeout, engine_malformed_input, engine_error, engine_unavailable — mapped to ErrResult {ok:false, code, message, retryable} semantics.
Existing 50-test suite remains green; new geometry tests are added (deterministic geometry set, worker isolation, host parity through the real adapter).
CI reproduces real-engine tests on the pinned candidate toolchain (OCCT 7.8.1.1 via cadquery-ocp, python3).
Evidence records exact engine/tool versions and any environment limitations.
No protected architecture paths are modified.
non_goals: IFC authoring/round-trip implementation (covered by CAD-003 research and a later production slice).
Architecture modification (Architecture v1.1 remains FROZEN; no protected path touched).
Construction Graph integration (CADDocument remains the editor representation; Graph mapping is a separate work item).
risk_assumptions: BRANCH STRATEGY (governance dependency note): CAD-IMPLEMENT-002 branches off work/cad-implement-001-app-shell (the CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 PR #25 branch) to inherit and inspect the CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 contracts and hosts, per the Architect directive step 1 ('Inspect the merged CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 contracts and hosts before changing them'). CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 is currently PR_OPEN (not yet VERIFIED); declaring it as a formal governance dependency would block execution under the VERIFIED-dependency rule, and no override mechanism exists. The Architect's execution directive on Issue #26 (comment 5421265944) explicitly authorizes implementation now, so the declared dependencies are the VERIFIED items whose findings this work item consumes (ARCH-WF-001 governance foundation, RESEARCH-CAD-002 OCCT capability validation, RESEARCH-CAD-005 operational/performance findings). When CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 merges and is VERIFIED, this branch rebases onto main and the code-level dependency becomes explicit. This choice is recorded here for Architect visibility, not hidden.

ENGINE CHOICE (OCCT via cadquery-ocp, not the FreeCAD AppImage): the validated candidate toolchain per RESEARCH-CAD-005 is OCCT 7.8.1.1 (cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1) + FreeCAD 1.1.3. The FreeCAD 1.1.3 AppImage is not present in the execution environment (only its recorded SHA256); OCCT 7.8.1.1 IS present and importable (from OCP import BRepPrimAPI, BRepAlgoAPI, gp works). The real adapter therefore uses the OCCT kernel directly through the OCP Python bindings in an isolated subprocess worker — the same kernel FreeCAD itself uses. engineId is 'occt' (not 'freecad'), engineVersion records the exact cadquery-ocp/OCCT version. FreeCAD-native document formats (FCStd) are NOT required by the minimum geometry set (box, cylinder, transform, boolean fuse/cut).

GEOMETRY-PREPARE APP API EXTENSION (additive): the current AppApiHandler never invokes GeometryEngineAdapter.prepareGeometry or BimEngineAdapter.extractSemantics (only file.read/file.write are exercised — confirmed by inspection of the CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 contracts). To make real geometry flow through the shared App API on both hosts without changing the existing command semantics, CAD-IMPLEMENT-002 adds ONE new command 'geometry.prepare' (additive CommandName extension + AJV schema + dispatch case). The EngineAdapterBundle contract itself is byte-unchanged. Existing commands and the existing 50 tests are untouched (they never send geometry.prepare). The renderer/CADDocument/App API core gain zero engine imports. If the Architect considers even this additive extension out of scope, it is removable without affecting the adapter implementation.

DETERMINISM CONTRACT (host parity + render determinism): OCCT geometry is deterministic for identical inputs (same recipe -> same shape -> same tessellation). The adapter derives meshToken as 'occt:' + SHA-256 over a canonical encoding of the tessellated mesh (sorted vertex coordinates + triangle indices, fixed decimal formatting), so identical geometry recipes produce identical meshTokens across processes, runs, and hosts — preserving the LOCK-017 deterministic-scene-hash and host-parity invariants. Geometry results are deterministic within declared tolerances (OCCT computes in doubles; the canonical encoding rounds coordinates to 1e-9 to absorb last-bit float noise).

WORKER ISOLATION (CAD-005 §5-§7 constraints, mandatory): the engine runs in a disposable Python subprocess per prepareGeometry call (process-per-call isolation — CAD-005 measured it affordable at every tier). The Node-side adapter enforces: wall-clock timeout at the process boundary with SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation (in-process cancellation is impossible for native OCCT calls — measured); optional RLIMIT_AS address-space ceiling per worker; structural validation of worker responses (checksums/shape counts, never trusting reader success blindly); bounded boolean decomposition is NOT required for the minimum set (single-tool fuse/cut only) but the timeout bounds runaway booleans; typed failures (engine_timeout, engine_malformed_input, engine_error, engine_unavailable) mapped to the App API ErrResult convention with retryable flags.

DUMMY ADAPTER PERMANENCE: the dummy adapter is NOT removed, modified, or demoted — it remains the deterministic test double for the whole existing suite (50 tests) and for future engine-independent tests. The real OCCT adapter is additive (new package app/src/adapters/occt/), wired into the deployable hosts (apps/web, apps/electron) per the directive ('Connect the Web and Electron workspace surfaces to the real adapter through the same App API').

SPEC DIVERGENCE (same pattern as CAD-IMPLEMENT-001): spec/work-items.md defines PLATFORM-006 as the closest frozen ancestor; CAD-IMPLEMENT-002 is defined by Issue #26 as the CAD-IMPLEMENT-* production track continuation. The implementer follows Issue #26 as the authoritative execution definition and flags the divergence.

ENVIRONMENT LIMITATIONS (recorded per acceptance criteria): the real-engine tests require python3 with cadquery-ocp (OCCT 7.8.1.1) importable. Locally this is /home/z/.venv (python 3.12.13, cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1). CI installs the pinned toolchain (python3 + pip install cadquery-ocp==7.8.1.1.post1). Tests that require the engine are SKIPPED (not failed) with an explicit marker when the engine is absent, so environments without the engine still run the full non-engine suite — the skip reason is recorded in the test output and evidence.

evidence.description: Deterministic real-engine test suite (the core acceptance evidence). The app/ suite grows 50 -> 74 tests, ALL RUNNING against the pinned real toolchain (python 3.12.13 + cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1 = OCCT 7.8.1.1, the CAD-005-validated kernel; no FreeCAD AppImage required for the minimum geometry set). 24 new tests in three files: (1) app/test/occt-geometry.test.ts — the minimum canonical geometry set: box (deterministic meshToken occt:0f067e615f4739e713d836a915b0e571fcb27fcb4838e8d3dd8b588af7abc3eb for box 2x3x4, identical across calls, adapter instances and processes; volume exactly 24; 8 vertices / 12 triangles; bbox within the declared 0.01 tolerance), cylinder (volume pi*r^2*h within 1e-6; gp_Ax2 base-center axis semantics verified; determinism), transform (translation/rotation/uniform-scale bbox correctness; rigid transforms preserve volume exactly), boolean fuse (disjoint volumes add; overlapping union 8 + pi*0.25*0.5 within 1e-4; determinism), boolean cut (8 - pi*0.25*1.5 within 1e-4; nested cut+transform composition; rigid transform preserves volume), bundle wiring (all three sub-adapter marks; file round-trip preserves the occt: meshToken; BIM passthrough + shared kernel version). (2) app/test/occt-worker-isolation.test.ts — the CAD-005 operational findings enforced at the process boundary: wall-clock timeout fires at the process boundary with typed retryable engine_timeout; the disposable worker RECOVERS after a timeout kill (the next call succeeds on a fresh process); missing python runtime -> engine_unavailable; missing worker script -> engine_unavailable; unparseable worker output -> engine_error (never trusted blindly); crashing worker -> engine_error; stdout noise before the JSON line tolerated (last-line fallback); descriptor compile failures typed engine_malformed_input WITHOUT spawning (11 malformed-descriptor cases). (3) app/test/geometry-prepare.test.ts — the additive geometry.prepare command through the shared AppApiHandler: dummy bundle degrades gracefully (dummy meshToken, null mesh/metadata); prepare is non-mutating (content hash unchanged); bad payload -> bad_payload; OCCT compile failures map to engine_malformed_input (engine NOT required for these — they run everywhere); idempotency key honored; the real result carries meshToken + bbox + mesh (8 verts) + metadata (volume 24) + engine occt@7.8.1.1.post1; determinism through the command layer; the result persists through the EXISTING applyEdit(addElement) workflow; typed timeout surfaces engine_timeout retryable verbatim; THE HOST-PARITY TEST: the same representative geometry workflow (prepare box -> add -> prepare fuse(box,cylinder) -> add -> setSelection -> undo -> redo) through WebHost(WebSocketTransport) AND ElectronHost(IpcTransport) with the REAL OCCT adapter yields IDENTICAL meshTokens AND identical CADDocument content hashes AND identical deterministic scene hashes (LOCK-017). The existing 50-test suite is untouched and green (dummy adapter unchanged, byte-identical). Full suite: 74/74 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped (engine present).
evidence.reproduction: cd app && node --import tsx --test test/*.test.ts (74 pass with python3 + cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1 on PATH; engine-required tests skip with a recorded reason when the toolchain is absent).

evidence.description: The real OCCT adapter + model viewport implementation (inspectable source). REAL ADAPTER: app/src/adapters/occt/ — worker/occt-worker.py (the isolated Python OCCT worker: one JSON request on stdin -> one JSON response on stdout per disposable process; box/cylinder(gp_Ax2 axis)/transform(row-major 4x4 affine)/boolean fuse-cut recipe DAG with full structural validation, 256-step and 2M-vertex bounds; deterministic meshToken = 'occt:' + SHA-256 over the canonical encoding of the deduplicated+sorted tessellated mesh (fixed 9-decimal formatting, negative-zero normalized); tolerance-inclusive OCCT Bnd_Box bbox; GProp volume; typed failures engine_malformed_input/engine_error/engine_unavailable), occt-process.ts (the Node driver: process-per-call spawn; wall-clock timeout with SIGTERM->SIGKILL escalation; 64MiB bounded output; prlimit RLIMIT_AS ceiling when OFFISOS_OCCT_RLIMIT_AS is set; structural validation of every worker response — token shape, bbox finiteness, mesh index ranges; OFFISOS_PYTHON/OFFISOS_OCCT_WORKER overrides + cwd-based worker resolution for app/, repo root and both hosts), occt-geometry-adapter.ts (GeometryEngineAdapter implementation + the recursive GeometryDescriptor -> flat recipe compiler with depth/step bounds — compilation IS validation, malformed descriptors are typed before any spawn; bounded 64-entry mesh cache; MeshProvider.describeMesh + GeometryMetadataProvider.describeGeometryMetadata optional capabilities; live engineVersion getter), occt-bim-adapter.ts (documented passthrough — IfcOpenShell is a later production slice per Issue #26 non-goals), occt-file-adapter.ts (format 'offisos-occt', canonical Offisos JSON — deterministic adapter-state serialization sufficient for the existing CADDocument save/open workflow), index.ts (createOcctAdapterBundle). ADDITIVE APP API EXTENSION: app/src/contracts/geometry.ts (NEW file — GeometryDescriptor/MeshData/GeometryMetadata types, AdapterFailure typed-failure class with codes engine_timeout/engine_unavailable/engine_error/engine_malformed_input, structural MeshProvider/GeometryMetadataProvider capability checks — engine-free, LOCK-018 clean); app/src/contracts/app-api.ts gains ONE CommandName 'geometry.prepare' (additive per api-contract.md §8; the EngineAdapterBundle contract app/src/contracts/adapter.ts is BYTE-UNCHANGED); app/src/app-api/schema.ts gains the recursive $defs geometry-descriptor AJV schema; app/src/app-api/contract.ts gains cmdPrepareGeometry (typed AdapterFailure -> ErrResult mapping; structural result validation; optional mesh/metadata attachment). HOST WIRING (LOCK-003 proven — the bundle swap is the ONLY change): apps/web/src/app/api/cad/route.ts and apps/electron/src/main/main.ts swap DummyAdapterBundle -> createOcctAdapterBundle() (lazy worker — commands that never prepare geometry run engine-free; the CAD-IMPLEMENT-001 electron smoke still passes WITHOUT python installed). MODEL VIEWPORT: apps/web/src/app/page.tsx + apps/electron/src/renderer/workspace.ts both gain Box (OCCT)/Cylinder (OCCT)/Fuse (OCCT) buttons driving geometry.prepare -> applyEdit(addElement) through the SAME App API, an isometric SVG model viewport (painter-sorted flat-shaded triangles projected from the real tessellated mesh — host-surface presentation only; the shared renderer core still consumes just meshToken+transform for the LOCK-017 scene hash), deterministic mesh re-hydration from props.geometry on reload, and an engine badge (occt 7.8.1.1.post1). The client transports gain prepareGeometry wrappers (apps/web/src/cad/client/http-transport.ts; the Electron preload already passes any command through window.cad.send).

evidence.description: Reproducible real-engine Electron + Web host evidence. ELECTRON GEOMETRY SMOKE (apps/electron/test/smoke-geometry.mjs, npm run smoke:geometry — additive; the CAD-001 smoke test/smoke.mjs stays byte-identical and still passes engine-free): launches Xvfb, runs electron --no-sandbox --smoke-geometry, drives the FULL Issue #26 chain THROUGH the real BrowserWindow via webContents.executeJavaScript — 10/10 steps PASS on Electron 33.4.11 / Node 20.18.3 / Chrome 130.0.6723.191: (1) geometry.prepare box -> meshToken occt:0f067e615f4739e713d836a915b0e571fcb27fcb4838e8d3dd8b588af7abc3eb, 8 verts, engine occt@7.8.1.1.post1; (2) volume exactly 24 + bbox within tolerance; (3) fuse(box 4x3x2, cylinder r=1 h=5 at (2,1.5,0)) -> token occt:e9b79c7760fc6058eeb0a402260b9b2ca90ace22118dea1d92e252e435388b5b, volume 33.424777961; (4) determinism — repeated prepare returns the IDENTICAL token; (5) applyEdit(addElement) with the real occt: token through the native IPC; (6) getState has 1 element carrying the token; (7) setSelection/getSelection metadata on the real element; (8) undo reverts it; (9) redo restores it; (10) typed failure: malformed descriptor -> engine_malformed_input retryable=false. The result JSON persists to apps/electron/dist/smoke-geometry-result.json for CI artifact upload. WEB HOST BROWSER VERIFICATION (dev server, agent-browser): the workspace at / hydrates and the 'Add real OCCT box'/'Add real OCCT cylinder'/'Fuse real OCCT box and cylinder' buttons drive geometry.prepare -> applyEdit through fetch('/api/cad') — after the workflow the canvas renders 654 shaded mesh polygons (the isometric model viewport of real engine geometry: cylinder + fused solid), the engine badge reads 'occt 7.8.1.1.post1', document.getState shows the elements with occt: meshTokens, undo reverts the last element, and the browser console shows ZERO errors. A direct curl of POST /api/cad with the box descriptor returns meshToken occt:0f067e615f4739e713d836a915b0e571fcb27fcb4838e8d3dd8b588af7abc3eb — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Electron host's token (live cross-host determinism through the real engine).
evidence.reproduction: cd apps/electron && npm run smoke:geometry (Xvfb required; 10/10 steps, exit 0). Web: cd apps/web && npm run dev (port 3000), open http://localhost:3000 (localhost, NOT 127.0.0.1 — Next.js 16 blocks cross-origin HMR from 127.0.0.1 in dev), click 'Box (OCCT)' / 'Cylinder (OCCT)' / 'Fuse (OCCT)', observe the isometric mesh viewport + engine badge, click Undo. Direct API: curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/cad -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"api":"1","body":{"type":"command","name":"geometry.prepare","payload":{"geometry":{"shape":"box","width":2,"depth":3,"height":4}}}}' (deterministic occt: token).

evidence_requirements: Deterministic automated test suite proving the real-engine geometry set (box, cylinder, transform, boolean fuse/cut) with identical meshTokens/bboxes across repeated runs and both hosts, reproducible from the committed source on the pinned toolchain.

Worker-isolation evidence: timeout enforcement, typed failures (engine_timeout, engine_malformed_input, engine_error, engine_unavailable), process-level cancellation, and recovery after a killed worker.
Adapter-boundary evidence: EngineAdapterBundle contract byte-unchanged; forbidden-import static check (LOCK-018) green; dummy adapter and the existing 50-test suite untouched and green.
Host-parity evidence: the same geometry workflow through WebHost and ElectronHost transports yields identical results, bound to the implementation revision.
Engine-version evidence: exact OCCT/cadquery-ocp/Python versions recorded, plus any environment limitations (engine-absent skip behavior).
CI workflow reproducing the real-engine tests on ubuntu-latest with the pinned toolchain installed.
No claim of VERIFIED; the implementer produces evidence and submits for Architect review (LOCK-004: implementation status is not evidence).
